title: What If You Could Buy Weather In Space?

publish.title: What If You Could BUY Weather On Mars? #shorts
publish.description: What if kids on a space colony with no weather at all could buy snow, rainbows and storms from a vending machine? Which weather would you order first?
publish.caption: What if you could buy weather in space? 🚀🌈

scenes.line: What if you could *buy* weather in space?
scenes.title: WHAT IF...

scenes.line: I grew up on a space colony. We have no weather. *None*.
Every day is exactly the *same*. Dusty. Still. Boring.
My brother Max has never seen *rain*.
Then a strange ship landed. It sold *weather*.
Sunshine, one coin. Snow, two. Storms, *half* price.
I had exactly one *coin*. I bought snow.
And it actually *snowed*. On a space colony.
Max caught one on his tongue. He screamed with *joy*.
The whole colony wanted more. So we *all* started buying.
Mia bought a *rainbow* for her birthday.
The mayor bought glowing lights for the whole *sky*.
Somebody ordered wind. Just to fly a *kite*.
Best month of my *life*.
But nobody read the tiny words on the *receipt*.
It said: weather does not come with an *off* button.
My snow never stopped. It became a *blizzard*.
The wind met the dust. Hello, *sandstorm*.
Then somebody's cheap storm kicked *in*.
And the glowing sky turned dark *red*.
We had wanted weather. We got all of it. At *once*.
I ran to the ship. The salesman was *packing*.
He said refunds cost extra. So I made him a *deal*.
Take it all back, and we will give you *something* better.
He had been flying alone for nine hundred *years*.
So we offered him a home. And a job as our *weatherman*.
He turned everything off. Then gave us *one* a day.
Snow on Mondays. Rainbows on *Fridays*.
And every year, on Max's birthday, it *rains*.
The storms? Still half price. Nobody is *buying*.
